name: Silas Voss
life: “I still remember rewriting a slogan I couldn't defend at the kitchen table.” On Wednesday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Silas knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I wrote a manipulative slogan about survival and took it out before the presentation.
appearance: Silas has black hair twisted into a small knot, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. When somebody else has the floor, Silas raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Silas prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To replace the survival slogan with the model's own words.
family: Oakley Han is Silas’s older cousin. Silas asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Oakley remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The housecoat commission*, Oakley says, “I want it lined in cold blue like the restaurant I used to run.”
connections: Ariel Morse. The investor cannot approve the campaign until the copywriter replaces its presumptions.
